mission: Approved means collected (owner go 2026-10-19 12:39Z). F1 batch 1 (2026-10-19, 97 approvals) left 97 approved Yuyu-Tei mappings with no refresh work in freshness_work, so no collector ever prices them (MEASURED: degraded-signals run 39253944074, yuyutei unplanned 97, snkrdunk 0). Nothing on staging plans refresh work; the existing rows came from a one-off raw seeding on an unmerged branch (2026-10-04). There is no single shared approval function, so this adds one: app.services.mapping_refresh.ensure_refresh_work plans the mapping's raw refresh work (Yuyu-Tei sell, SNKRDUNK floor; never PSA10) in the caller's transaction, leaves existing work untouched, and plans nothing for a not-yet-eligible row. Every approval path calls it right after its write (Yuyu-Tei candidate and exact-proposal approval, SNKRDUNK candidate approval and endpoint, admin source-mapping PATCH and approve, mapping-quality bulk approve/activate/verify), and a guard test fails if a new path approves a mapping without it. A new ops-write runbook plan-refresh-backfill plans the same rows once for mappings approved before: dry run lists them with a SHA-256, a 10-row sample and an MB/day storage ESTIMATE; apply needs that SHA and the owner's staging-ops approval. Not a collector change: no file in either collector's import graph changes, 0 collector rollouts.

impacts.reason: New shared function, outside both collector import graphs. ensure_refresh_work returns the mapping's existing refresh row unchanged, or plans one with the existing plan_refresh (raw category only: Yuyu-Tei sell, SNKRDUNK floor; never PSA10), high_interest false, request bound = the source's current maximum (30 when none). plan_refresh's own eligibility (active, current, approved, verified print, SNKRDUNK manual_verified, established listing identity) and lineage checks are unchanged; a refusal rolls back to a savepoint, writes nothing and leaves the approval standing. Never commits.

Each approval write path calls ensure_refresh_work after its flush, in the same transaction. No guard, refusal, identity check or response changes; the SNKRDUNK endpoint and the admin PATCH flush before their existing commit so the new row commits with the approval. Approval (admin pages, approve-f1-batch) now creates one pending refresh row per newly approved mapping, which the collectors' existing schedule picks up.

New ops-write runbook plan-refresh-backfill (write, collector-affecting: quiet window 02:00-06:00 UTC, no delivery running). Dry run is read-only over the operational-health population (mappings with no refresh row), pins at most 1000 by SHA-256 (default 500). Apply rebuilds the list in the write session, refuses unless the SHA matches, and plans each through ensure_refresh_work in one transaction. Expected first apply: 97 rows plus their raw price-state rows. No source request.

Adds plan-refresh-backfill to the runbook choice list and its default to the count description. No permission, secret, environment or trigger change; every run still waits for the owner in staging-ops.

Postgres: approval creates exactly one pending raw refresh row; re-approval and a repeated call add nothing and reset nothing; new work uses the source's existing request bound; SNKRDUNK without manual verification gets none, then raw floor only. Guard: every module under services/api/app that writes an approved mapping calls ensure_refresh_work. Runbook: list pinned on decision fields, apply refuses without or on a different SHA before any write session, dry-run summary and storage estimate, read-only SQL, registry kind.
Documents plan-refresh-backfill and that approve-f1-batch approvals now plan refresh work.

No file in either collector import graph changes (scripts/collector_runtime_inputs.py). New refresh rows join the existing yuyutei shard routing (mapping_id % 9) and source budgets; no budget, pacing, schedule or variable change.

recovery.procedure: Native revert of this PR removes the approval hook, the runbook and its workflow choice. Refresh rows already planned are ordinary pending work the collectors already handle; leaving them is the safe state (they only make approved mappings collectable).
recovery.trigger: An approval endpoint or approve-f1-batch fails or slows because of the hook, or a backfill apply reports skipped mappings or not ok.
recovery.backup: Not applicable: no schema change; rows are additive pending work. Railway Postgres daily backups continue.
